THE NSX GT3 RACECAR WAS ALWAYS PART OF THE PLAN.
When the second-generation NSX was approved for development, Acura engineers
wasted no time putting pen to paper. Racing was foremost on their minds. The NSX
production car and its GT3 sibling were created in tandem with a shared vision: That
‘ 9 1
of a sophisticated supercar with bare-knuckles racing chops.
Development began in Japan and Europe, where the first NSX GT3 was built and
prepped for testing. From there, it moved to Santa Clarita, California - headquarters
of Honda Performance Development (HPD), Acura’s North American race
engineering group, for further development and entry into racing competition.
The NSX GT3 completed FIA homologation in 2016, allowing it to compete in the
2017 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and Pirelli World Challenge
series. During this first year, the NSX GT3 led its class during the prestigious 24
Hours of Daytona, and secured wins with the Michael Shank Racing Team at
Detroit's Belle Isle Grand Prix and Watkins Glen International Raceway in New York.
The track success of the new GT3 is the latest chapter in a storied racing legacy,
and testament to the importance the Acura brand places on producing and
perfecting high-performance automobiles.
For the first time in Acura’s history, a factory-developed race vehicle will be available
to qualified customers. The race-ready, twin-turbo NSX GT3 supercar can be
purchased through HPD, which will offer customer support, including parts sales
and engineering assistance.
